subject: On‑prem perimeter credentialing: egress proofs & firewall rule signoff
body:
From: Chris Alvarez <chris@novacorp.com>
To: david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: it-security@novacorp.com, procurement@novacorp.com
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: On‑prem perimeter credentialing: sample evidence needed for private runtime

Hi David —

Thanks again for walking our cloud & security team through the private runtime options last week. To close our internal audit for Private Deployment (on‑prem) we need a short packet showing the following for Redwood’s private endpoint (control plane + runtime):

- Egress origin IPs or stable FQDNs that outbound traffic will come from (control plane callbacks, model updates, telemetry).
- Minimal firewall policy snippets (ports/protocols) for our perimeter team to apply on the tenant gateway.
- A lightweight evidence CSV that maps each egress destination to purpose and expected frequency.
- Any fallback behaviors (e.g., regional mirrors, model variant switchover) that change origin IPs.

Can you provide those artifacts and a one‑page note on how Redwood treats KV/prefix caching with respect to egress (does cache sync occur outbound)? We want to avoid overbroad 0.0.0.0/0 rules.

Also copying our procurement lead — they’ll need a short paragraph describing operational responsibilities so we can map contract scope.

Cheers,
Chris
Chris Alvarez
Head of Cloud Architecture, NovaCorp

---

From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: Chris Alvarez <chris@novacorp.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On‑prem perimeter credentialing: sample evidence needed for private runtime

Chris —

Appreciate the clear checklist. Attaching a short packet (network diagram + CSV + draft rules) — see attachments. High level answers inline: 

1) Egress origins: Redwood’s control plane callbacks for private deployments originate from a set of stable IPs we reserve per region plus optional customer‑specific NAT candidates when using a managed connector. For NovaCorp (US‑west) the planned origin set for control/telemetry is: 52.23.14.120, 52.23.14.121, 34.210.44.9. These represent the control plane egress. Model cache fetches (large model blobs) will be pulled from regionally replicated object stores; their IPs are announced in the attached CSV and are stable within the release window.

2) Firewall snippets (suggested):
- Outbound TCP 443 to the control plane IP set (above) — allow from private runtime subnet(s).
- Outbound TCP 443 to model artifact FQDNs (cdn.rw-models-us-west.redwood.com) — prefer FQDN allowlist; fallback to resolved IPs in our CSV if FQDNs not supported.
- Outbound UDP 53 to your DNS resolvers only.

3) Evidence CSV: contains columns (dst_ip_or_fqdn, purpose, expected_daily_requests, uses_tls, notes). See egress-evidence.csv.

4) Fallbacks: if a regional mirror is used during outages, the origin FQDN will shift to mirror-us-west.rw-models.redwood.com; that is included in the CSV and the mirror uses the same TLS certs. We do not perform KV cache synces that leak private prompt data — KV/prefix caches are local to the runtime and only metadata about keys (not values) is ever sent for metadata reconciliation; we include a short note about that in the packet.

Operational responsibilities (for procurement): Redwood operates the control plane and is responsible for publishing origin IPs and timely notification for any planned rotation. NovaCorp is responsible for applying the outbound rules on tenant perimeter devices and maintaining the local egress NAT. If NovaCorp requires static single IP egress (IP whitelisting), we can provide an optional managed NAT with dedicated IPs under a dedicated capacity addendum.

Attaching: novacorp_network_diagram_v2.pdf, egress-evidence.csv, firewall-rules-draft.txt

—David
David Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

---

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 11:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On‑prem perimeter credentialing: sample evidence needed for private runtime

David / team —

Quick comments after reviewing the attachments:

- The CSV looks good but we should mark the control plane IPs as subject to rotation with a 30‑day notice window. NovaCorp asked for "stable" values — let's be explicit in the header that these are current allocations (not SLA guarantees) unless we accept the managed NAT addendum.
- Firewall snippet: add explicit egress socket timeout guidance for long‑lived streams (we recommend idle timeout >= 5m for streaming APIs to avoid premature termination).
- Add a small note about telemetry minimization: we transmit request metrics and status codes; we do not transmit raw request payloads unless the customer opts into enhanced telemetry.

I drafted a short one‑paragraph operational blurb for procurement (below) — please sign off before I pass to legal/procurement.

Operational paragraph (draft):
"Redwood Inference will publish and maintain a publicly accessible manifest of origin FQDNs and IP allocations used for private deployments. Redwood operates the control plane and is responsible for outbound endpoint availability and notification of planned IP rotations. The customer (NovaCorp) is responsible for applying and maintaining outbound firewall rules and NAT mappings on their perimeter devices, and for ensuring DNS resolution of Redwood‑published FQDNs. If the customer requires single‑IP whitelisting, Redwood can provide a managed NAT option under a separate commercial agreement."

If that looks good I’ll send the packet to Chris + IT Security with a pointed note on rotation policy.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

---

From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: Chris Alvarez <chris@novacorp.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, it-security@novacorp.com, procurement@novacorp.com
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On‑prem perimeter credentialing: sample evidence needed for private runtime

Chris —

Uploading the finalized packet to the shared Drive and confirming next steps:

1) Attached artifacts (also copied to the Drive link): network diagram, CSV evidence, firewall snippets, and a short FAQ about caching/telemetry.
2) We marked the control plane IPs as "current allocations; rotate with 30‑day notice" in the CSV header. If NovaCorp needs guaranteed static egress IPs, let us know and we’ll scope the managed NAT option and price it as an addendum.
3) We recommend the following minimal firewall rule set (apply from runtime subnets):
   - Allow TCP/443 to 52.23.14.120, 52.23.14.121, 34.210.44.9 (control plane)
   - Allow TCP/443 to cdn.rw-models-us-west.redwood.com (model artifact downloads)
   - Allow UDP/53 to your DNS resolvers only
   - Allow ICMP echo replies only (for health checks)
   - Set idle timeout >= 5 minutes for streaming sessions

4) Action items for NovaCorp team: confirm whether FQDN allowlisting is acceptable or if you require resolved IPs; confirm whether you want the managed NAT single‑IP option.

If procurement needs the short paragraph for the SOW, Laura’s draft is below (we’re happy to adjust language for legal).

Operational paragraph: "Redwood Inference will publish and maintain a manifest of origin FQDNs and IP allocations used for private deployments. Redwood operates the control plane and is responsible for outbound endpoint availability and notification of planned IP rotations. The customer (NovaCorp) is responsible for applying and maintaining outbound firewall rules and NAT mappings on their perimeter devices, and for ensuring DNS resolution of Redwood‑published FQDNs. If the customer requires single‑IP whitelisting, Redwood can provide a managed NAT option under a separate commercial agreement."

Next: Laura will send the final packet to your IT Security team with the rotation clarification unless you want us to hold.

Thanks —
David

Attachments: novacorp_network_diagram_v2.pdf (diagram), egress-evidence.csv (csv), firewall-rules-draft.txt (plain text)
